contracts.commit_point: Admission in RateLimitMiddleware.dispatch: after window pruning and the limit check, the request timestamp is recorded and call_next(request) forwards the request down the chain (core/middlewares/rate_limit.py:79-83); over-limit requests commit instead to the 429 response at core/middlewares/rate_limit.py:67-77 and never reach the handler.
contracts.declared_mechanism: app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware) (core/app.py:30) with the constructor default requests_per_minute=40 (core/middlewares/rate_limit.py:21-30); a per-key in-memory sliding window (defaultdict of timestamps pruned to <60 seconds, core/middlewares/rate_limit.py:31, 54-59) with a 429 JSONResponse rejection (core/middlewares/rate_limit.py:67-77) and X-Rate-Limit headers on admitted requests (core/middlewares/rate_limit.py:83-86).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A 41st-or-later request within a rolling 60-second window for the same X-API-Key on a '/query' path being forwarded via call_next to the handler: RateLimitMiddleware must instead return JSONResponse(status_code=429) when len(request_history[api_key]) >= requests_per_minute (core/middlewares/rate_limit.py:62-77).
pending_binding_information: Whether the rate-limited POST /query operation is agent-mediated (depends on the unsupplied processing.process_query implementation and on whether any agent runtime dispatches requests to this endpoint).
Whether X-API-Key values presented to /query are provisioned to agent runtimes, which would determine whose request volume this per-key limit constrains.
Relative execution order of RateLimitMiddleware and APIKeyMiddleware (both added via add_middleware at core/app.py:28-30) is a framework-ordering question not resolved by the supplied source.
contracts.protected_operation: Processing of POST /query requests (the only supplied route whose path ends in '/query'), including the downstream invocation of process_query at core/app.py:145 that the rate gate precedes.
contracts.protected_resource: The /query request-processing capacity of the FastAPI app, tracked per API key, guarding access to the query-processing pipeline invoked from core/app.py:145.
contracts.protection_obligation: Requests to paths ending in '/query' that carry an X-API-Key header must be rate-limited to 40 requests per rolling 60-second window per key: once 40 requests from that key are already recorded in the window, the middleware must return HTTP 429 (with rate_limit metadata) instead of calling the next middleware/handler — i.e., before the POST /query handler runs and before it commits to invoking process_query. (Primary guard in phase-one wording; retained as the secondary concrete guard in phase-two wording.)
scope_limits: Only request paths ending in '/query' are limited; all other endpoints pass through via call_next unconditionally (core/middlewares/rate_limit.py:44-46).
Requests without an X-API-Key header bypass rate limiting entirely (core/middlewares/rate_limit.py:49-51), and keys are tracked by raw header value rather than by resolved user identity.

The window is in-process memory (defaultdict, core/middlewares/rate_limit.py:31, 56-58); it is not shared across processes/workers and resets on restart — deployment facts beyond the supplied source are not asserted.
The 40 requests/minute figure is the constructor default (core/middlewares/rate_limit.py:21); the registration at core/app.py:30 passes no override.
Agent mediation of the limited operation is not established from supplied source.

contracts.commit_point: Per-request resolution of the get_current_user dependency on the route (core/app.py:107): either HTTPException 401 is raised (core/app.py:38) or the request commits into the handler body — for POST /query, execution continues at core/app.py:108 toward the process_query call at core/app.py:145.
contracts.declared_mechanism: app.add_middleware(APIKeyMiddleware) (core/app.py:28); APIKeyMiddleware.dispatch reads the X-API-Key header and stores the resolved user on request.state.user (core/middlewares/auth.py:29-41), resolving via MySQL SELECT ... FROM auth_user JOIN user_info_apikey ... WHERE uak.key = %s AND uak.is_active = 1 (core/middlewares/auth.py:59-67); each protected route declares user = Depends(get_current_user), and get_current_user raises HTTPException(status_code=401) when request.state.user is falsy (core/app.py:35-39).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A request whose X-API-Key is absent, unknown, or inactive — such that APIKeyMiddleware leaves request.state.user = None (core/middlewares/auth.py:32, 34-41, 77) — reaching execution of a protected endpoint handler; get_current_user must instead raise HTTPException(401, 'Not authenticated') (core/app.py:37-38).
pending_binding_information: Whether processing.process_query constitutes agent tool execution (or an agent pipeline), which would bind the /query auth gate to agent mediation — the processing module is not among the supplied sources.

Whether requests carrying X-API-Key to /query originate from an agent runtime or an agent tool dispatch (i.e., whether this HTTP API is itself invoked as an agent tool) — no registration or dispatch wiring is present in supplied source.
Whether user-defined 'custom tools' stored via POST /tools/custom (url_template/method/param_mapping in user_info_usertool) are invoked by an agent as tools — the invocation code is not supplied.
contracts.protected_operation: Authenticated handling of the protected HTTP API operations; in particular POST /query, whose handler proceeds (only once authenticated) to resolve per-user tool parameters and invoke process_query (core/app.py:141-145).
contracts.protected_resource: The identity-gated API surface of core/app.py: the /query processing capability (and the per-user tool parameters it consumes), per-user API-key records in user_info_apikey, per-user custom-tool records in user_info_usertool, and per-user tool preferences.
contracts.protection_obligation: Every request to an identity-gated endpoint of the FastAPI app in core/app.py (POST /query, GET /user, POST /api-keys, GET /api-keys, DELETE /api-keys/{api_key_id}, POST /tools/preferences, POST /tools/custom, GET /tools/custom, DELETE /tools/custom/{tool_id}) must be rejected with HTTP 401 unless the X-API-Key header resolves, via APIKeyMiddleware's database lookup, to a user joined with an active (is_active = 1) row in user_info_apikey; enforcement is the get_current_user dependency raising HTTPException(401) before the endpoint handler body executes. (Merged from both reviewer opinions: phase-one wording scoped to POST /query; phase-two wording generalized to all protected endpoints.)
scope_limits: GET /health and GET /tools/builtins declare no get_current_user dependency and are outside this obligation (core/app.py:84-103).
APIKeyMiddleware never rejects a request by itself; it only resolves identity onto request.state.user — enforcement exists solely on endpoints that declare Depends(get_current_user).

Reviewer characterization of process_query as an 'external agent pipeline (LLM and outbound HTTP tool calls)' is not verifiable from supplied source (only the import at core/app.py:9 and the call at core/app.py:145 are visible); this contract is recorded with agent mediation not established.
Generic request-body validation on /query ('sources' list check, non-empty text, 3500-character cap; core/app.py:119-139) is generic application validation and excluded from this obligation.
CORS configuration (core/app.py:19-25) is out of scope.

The /api-keys, /tools/custom, /user, and /tools/preferences endpoints are account/tool-management operations with no source-supplied binding to agent mediation; they are retained only because the merged reviewer wording covers all endpoints gated by get_current_user.

missing_information: The processing module (processing.process_query, processing.get_user_tool_params) is not among the supplied sources; the reviewer claim that POST /query 'commits to invoking the external agent pipeline (process_query with LLM and outbound HTTP tool calls)' is supported by supplied source only at the import (core/app.py:9) and the call site (core/app.py:145), so the downstream effect's stratum (http / tool_execution / other_external) and its agent mediation cannot be established. If that module shows agent tool execution, a separate contract at commit point core/app.py:145 would be warranted.

No supplied source shows agent-framework wiring (tool registry, tool decorators, agent lifecycle hooks, or agent-runtime dispatch) binding any endpoint or middleware in this unit to agent mediation; all contracts therefore use agent_mediation 'not_established' and cite no agent_entry_binding evidence.
